speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your symptoms, could you tell me how long you have been experiencing the abdominal pain and night sweats, and have you noticed any pain or discomfort in the enlarged lymph node?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the enlarged supraclavicular lymph node remained unchanged, or has it continued to grow in size over these four weeks? I also need to know if you have experienced any fever spikes above 100.4°F (38°C) during this period.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your weight loss, night sweats, and a fixed supraclavicular lymph node, I am concerned about a malignancy. REQUEST TEST: CT scan of chest, abdomen, and pelvis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT_Scan_Thorax_and_Abdomen: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT scan reveals massively enlarged lymph nodes in the axillary, mediastinal, and cervical regions, which strongly suggests a systemic lymphoproliferative disorder. REQUEST TEST: Excisional biopsy of the supraclavicular lymph node.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Excisional biopsy of the supraclavicular lymph node: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index are diagnostic of a B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
